newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - India wallows in directionless trade.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - India wallows in directionless trade.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) ended little changed in London in very thin trade.
"The market moved very little either way," said a trader.

The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed up 0.17 points at 61.31 points, with the premium over the local market at 12.08 percent after the Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index fell 14.29 points to 3,104.66.
"There was good two-way business in Reliance at $10.00 and some buying of Indian Hotels, while Gujarat Ambuja saw selling," said the trader.
Reliance closed up 13 cents at $9.75/$10.50 after the company's share transfer agent in India was suspended by the Securities and Exchange Board.
"It is not good news, but then again, it is not too serious," said a trader.
Reliance, India's largest quoted company, will release its first half earnings on Friday.
Indian Hotels added $1.00 to $20.50/$21.50, while Gujarat Ambuja ended unchanged at $8.00/$9.00, a premium of 6.83 percent over the local stock.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended down 0.36 points at 72.40, a premium of 27.64 percent over the local market after the Korea Composite Index rose 6.58 points to a provisional close of 835.19.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended down 0.69 points at 90.17, a premium of 2.07 percent over the locals after the Taiwan Weighted Index fell 65.12 points, or 0.98 percent, to 6,551.26.
"There was not a lot happening in Asia, either," said a trader.
